subject: Hosted API latency SLO: temporary operational safety net & measurement questions
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <alex@finco.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: ops@finco.com
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API latency SLO: planned migration spike and temporary measurement leniency request

Hi Irene,

Quick note from the FinCo SRE team — we’re rolling a cross-region migration the week of Aug 24 to consolidate traffic and expect a multi-hour ramp that will materially spike tail latency for a subset of our requests (mainly embeddings and long-completion chat). Our PM asked whether Redwood can provide a temporary operational "safety net" for latency SLOs while we execute the cutover.

Specifically we’re asking:
- Can p50/p95 targets be relaxed for a bounded window around the migration?
- Can the measurement window be adjusted (e.g., ignore scheduled migration windows or extend rolling-window aggregation) to avoid an SLA breach?

We can share traffic profiles, traces, and a short CSV snapshot of pre-cutover latencies. What evidence do you need and what’s Redwood’s standard operational playbook for short-term carveouts?

Attaching a preliminary snapshot (finco_latency_snapshot_20260815.csv) and a small graph (service_graph_20260815.png).

Thanks — Alex
Alex Ramos
SRE Lead, FinCo
alex@finco.com

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Alex Ramos <alex@finco.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency SLO: planned migration spike and temporary measurement leniency request

Alex — thanks for the heads-up and for the attachments, those are helpful. Short answer: yes, we can offer a timebound operational safety net in coordination with you, but we'll need to formalize the scope, evidence, and rollback criteria. A few quick points to set expectations: 

1) Measurement approach: our hosted API p50/p95 are computed per-region on a rolling 24h window by default and reported as daily rollups. We can apply a localized carveout for scheduled migration windows or temporarily shift to a 7-day rolling baseline for the affected region(s).

2) Typical evidence we require:
   - Traffic profile (requests/sec by route) for the three days before the migration
   - Traces or span samples showing queueing vs execution time
   - Any known config changes (quantization, batch size, model switch) planned during the cutover

3) Timing/limit: we typically approve a provisional window of 7–14 days depending on severity; finance/CS and legal need to sign a short amendment for SLA exceptions beyond 48 hours.

Next steps from our side: I’ll loop in Ben (sales) and Marissa (CS/legal escalation) to surface the commercial and contractual path. If you can share the traffic profile CSV and an SRE dashboard link we’ll triage and propose a concrete carveout with conditions.

I’ll follow up with a proposed package by EOD tomorrow.

— Irene Choi
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API latency SLO: planned migration spike and temporary measurement leniency request

Forwarding FinCo’s request — they’ve attached a latency snapshot and graph. Proposed internal approach:

- Offer a provisional 7-day operational safety net covering Aug 19–Aug 26 for the affected region(s).
- Relax p50 to baseline * 1.2 and p95 to baseline * 2.0 for the provisional window; measure using the usual per-region rolling window but exclude scheduled maintenance windows flagged by the customer (we’ll need the exact time ranges).
- Conditions: customer provides live dashboard + CSV (they already sent a snapshot), keeps code/traffic plan static during the carveout except for the migration activities, and agrees to an amendment signed by Legal.

Evidence we should collect before we approve:
1) 72h request/sec heatmap by route
2) Representative trace set (top 5 slow traces)
3) Baseline p50/p95 for the prior 30 days

Commercial asks: Ben/Marissa — please advise on (a) crediting policy if SLOs are missed during the carveout, (b) whether we require a premium for the support window, and (c) the amendment template.

Karthik — any operational mitigations we should recommend to FinCo (e.g., pre-warming, cache priming, short-term increase in batch concurrency, model sharding)?

Irene

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 16:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API latency SLO: planned migration spike and temporary measurement leniency request

Thanks for looping us in. High-level position: we can support a provisional window but tighten the guardrails. My recommendations: 

- Approve a 7-day provisional carveout initially (Aug 19–26). If FinCo demonstrates a clear, unavoidable tail from their migration and provides requested telemetry, we can extend one additional 7-day period after a post-mortem.
- No automatic credits during carveout; if they request credits for impact outside the carveout period, handle via normal SLA claims process. If the p95 during the carveout exceeds 2x baseline persistently (>72h), we’ll trigger an operational remediation plan and provide a one-time credit (TBD, listed in pricing_impact_estimate.xlsx).
- Require signed amendment for any carveout longer than 48 hours.

Marissa — please prepare the amendment template and a redline that captures the temporary metric multipliers, the exact exclusion windows, and evidence requirements. I’ve attached an internal cost/impact estimate (pricing_impact_estimate.xlsx) for reference.

Ben
VP, Sales Operations

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Alex Ramos <alex@finco.com>, SRE Team <ops@finco.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Hosted API latency SLO — provisional safety net proposal and next steps

Alex — following internal review here’s a firmed-up path we can offer FinCo: 

1) Provisional window: Aug 19 00:00 UTC — Aug 26 23:59 UTC (7 days).
2) Metric relaxation: p50_target = baseline_p50 * 1.20; p95_target = baseline_p95 * 2.00 (baseline computed as median daily p50/p95 over prior 30 days).
3) Measurement: Redwood will continue per-region rolling 24h aggregation but will apply explicit carveouts for the scheduled migration windows you provide (precise timestamps). Outside the scheduled timestamps, measurement remains live.
4) Evidence required before start: 72h request/sec heatmap, representative traces (top 5 slow traces), and the 30-day baseline CSV (you’ve already provided a snapshot; please push the 30-day baseline to the Drive link).
5) Commercial/contract: 7-day carveout requires FinCo to sign a targeted amendment (DocuSign link: https://docu-sign.com/FINCO/SLAMOD). No automatic credits during the carveout. If p95 exceeds 2x baseline for a rolling 72h period during the carveout, we’ll: (a) open an operational incident with FinCo SREs, and (b) consider a one-time credit per the attached pricing estimate.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Aug 18 EOD: Redwood sends amendment template (Marissa) and our signed evidence checklist.
- Aug 19 00:00 UTC: Carveout begins provided evidence is uploaded and amendment signed.
- Aug 26 23:59 UTC: Carveout ends; follow-up post-mortem within 72h.

Please confirm you can provide the explicit migration timestamps and upload the 30-day baseline CSV to the Drive link. Once we have those, I’ll send the DocuSign for signature.

Thanks — let’s keep the channel open for any emergency coordination during the cutover.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: finco_latency_snapshot_20260815.csv (provided), service_graph_20260815.png (provided), slo_evidence_readme.pdf (packaging for our ops), pricing_impact_estimate.xlsx (internal)
